title: The Boy and the Filberts
summary: A hungry child grabs too many tasty treats and gets stuck.
coverScene: A young boy reaches inside a large glass jar filled with delicious brown nuts, while sunlight streams through a nearby window.

sentences.text: Once a young boy walked near a large house.
The boy looked inside a room.
A nice table stood in the room.

The item was full of food.
The food was sweet filberts.
The food was good and fine.
The boy saw the open item.
He wanted food very much.
He walked inside without fear.
He put his hand deep into the item.
His hand took many pieces of food.
He took as many pieces as he could hold.
He tried to pull his hand back out.
His closed hand was too big for the opening.
He could not pull his hand out of the item.
If he had taken fewer pieces, his hand would come out.
Instead, he held every single piece.
The poor boy stood by the table.
He felt very bad.
He did not know what to do.
He began to make a sound.

His problem caused a bad result.

The boy listened and dropped half of the food.

sentences.text: Once upon a time, a young boy walked near a large garden where a house stood.
Inside that house, a nice glass container was placed upon a brown table.
The container was completely filled with sweet nuts.
The young boy looked inside the room and saw the open container.
Because he wanted something good to eat, he walked inside without any fear.
He put his hand deep into the narrow neck of the glass container.
His fingers held as many food pieces as he could hold in his hand.
He tried to pull his hand back out with all the food.
However, his closed hand was now too big for the narrow opening.
He could not pull his hand out because the hole was too small.
If he had taken only a few pieces, his hand would have slipped back out.
Instead, he held onto every single piece that he had held.
The poor boy stood there by the table, feeling very sad and confused.
He began to cry a little bit because his hand was stuck fast.
His desire for too much had caused a funny problem which he could not solve alone.
After some time, a friend who lived in the house walked into the room.
The kind friend saw the boy standing by the table with his hand caught.
The good friend looked at the situation and gave him a simple piece of advice.
The person told the child to let go of half the food immediately.
The boy listened to this good suggestion and dropped half of the items.
As soon as his hand became smaller, his arm easily came out of the container.
He was finally free, and he still had enough food left to enjoy.
The child learned that taking less at one time is better than losing everything.
He has never forgotten this important lesson about life.
If he ever saw another open container, he would remember his past mistake.
His friend has also told other people about the funny event.
Everyone in the house now laughs when they talk about the day.
The young boy always shares his food with others now.
He has shared many meals since that day.
If he saw someone else in trouble, he would help them right away.

sentences.text: Once upon a time, a young boy walked near a large garden where a house stood.
Inside that house, a nice glass container was placed upon a wooden table.
The container was completely filled with a huge amount of wonderful sweet seeds.
The boy looked inside the room and saw the open container.
Because he wanted something good to eat, he walked inside without any fear.
He put his hand deep into the narrow neck of the glass container.
His fingers grabbed as many seeds as he could possibly hold in his hand.
He tried to pull his hand back out with all the food.
However, his closed hand filled with too many seeds was now too big for the narrow opening.
He could not pull his hand out because the glass hole was too small for such a big cluster.
If he had taken only a few seeds, his hand would have easily slipped back out.
Instead, he held onto every single piece that he had grabbed.
The poor boy stood there by the table, feeling very sad and confused.
He began to cry a little bit because his hand was stuck fast.
He could neither move his arm forward nor pull it away from the container.
His strong desire for food had caused a silly problem which he could not solve alone.
After some time, another person who lived in the house walked into the room.
The kind friend saw the boy standing by the table with his hand trapped.
The wise friend looked at the situation and gave him a very simple piece of advice.
The person told the child to let go of half the seeds immediately.
The boy listened to this good suggestion and dropped half of the seeds from his hand.
As soon as his hand became smaller, his hand easily came out of the container.
He was finally free, and he still had enough wonderful food left to enjoy.
The child learned that taking less at one time is often much better than losing everything.

If a person wants too much at once, trouble will surely follow.
Wise people always understand that sharing and careful control bring peace.

Whenever he faced a difficult choice, he remembered the stuck hand.
He would smile and think about how little things matter when freedom is safe.

This particular story about the glass container and the seeds has traveled through many generations.

That kind of intense drive can blind us to obvious solutions.
If the boy had only let go of the extra seeds sooner, he would have avoided all that pain.

sentences.text: Twilight had begun to stretch long shadows across the quiet valley when the young boy wandered near the grand estate. Behind the wrought iron fence stood a magnificent garden, tended with meticulous care and bordered by an ancient stone wall. Within the stately house that rose beyond the greenery, a polished wooden table sat bathed in the fading amber light of late afternoon. Resting upon its heavy surface was a clear glass vessel of remarkable beauty, catching the dying sunbeams in its curves. To the wandering child, peering intently through the open window, the object of greatest fascination was the abundance contained within.

The heavy glass jar was filled to the brim with sweet roasted filberts, their rich brown shells gleaming faintly through the smooth walls. Having spent the afternoon running through the dusty lanes, the boy felt a sharp pang of hunger grip his stomach. Without a second thought for the boundaries of privacy or property, he slipped through the open casement window into the silent room. His bare feet made no sound against the polished floorboards as he approached the heavy table like a shadow. His eyes remained fixed upon the delicious prize, completely blind to anything beyond the immediate gratification of his appetite.

With breathless anticipation, he thrust his hand deep down into the narrow neck of the glass container. His eager fingers stretched wide, scraping against the hard sides of the jar as they plunged toward the bottom. There lay the sweet harvest, piled richly in a dense mound that promised an absolute feast. Without hesitation, he curled his fingers inward, scooping up as many filberts as his palm could possibly press together. He grabbed a massive handful, confident that his prize was secure within his grip. Triumph filled his chest as he prepared to pull the heavy harvest back out into the open air.

Yet, the moment he attempted to withdraw his arm, a sudden and stubborn obstacle brought his movement to a dead halt. His tightly clenched fist, bulging with the heavy cluster of nuts, was now significantly wider than the narrow opening of the jar. No matter how hard he pulled, his knuckles jammed firmly against the rigid glass rim, refusing to pass through. The neck of the container had not changed its dimensions, but his own greed had transformed his hand into an inescapable trap. Panic fluttered in his chest as he tugged harder, pulling with all his might against the unyielding barrier.

The afternoon silence of the room was broken only by the sound of his frantic breathing and the dull scrape of skin against glass. He pulled left, then right, twisting his wrist at awkward angles, but the narrow neck held him fast in its transparent grip. Had he been willing to sacrifice even a fraction of his haul, his hand would have slipped out effortlessly into the freedom of the room. Instead, driven by an unyielding impulse of acquisition, he held on desperately to every single nut he had initially seized. Not a single filbert would he willingly surrender to the floor, even as his predicament grew increasingly dire.

The initial thrill of the harvest dissolved rapidly into a cold realization of helplessness and sharp physical discomfort. Tears welled in his eyes, hot and sudden, tracing clean paths down his dust-stained cheeks as he stood trapped beside the heavy wooden table. He could neither push his arm back down to release his grip nor pull it upward to escape the glass prison. His own stubborn desire had forged invisible chains that bound him securely to the spot. Every second that ticked by felt like an eternity, magnifying his foolishness in the empty, echoing room.

Footsteps sounded softly from the hallway outside, breaking the heavy stillness that had settled over the distressed child. A resident of the house, a person of gentle demeanor and quiet wisdom, stepped into the sunlit room to investigate the faint noises. Pausing by the doorway, the visitor took in the strange scene with a calm and understanding gaze. The boy stood frozen beside the table, his arm raised at an awkward angle, weeping quietly into the empty space. It required no great detective work to comprehend the nature of the crisis that had befallen the young intruder.

Approaching with slow and reassuring steps, the kind friend offered neither scolding nor harsh judgment for the intrusion. Instead, pointing gently toward the trapped hand within the narrow glass neck, the wise observer offered a remarkably simple solution. The advice was as brief as it was profound: let go of half the nuts immediately, and the problem would vanish. The boy stared at the speaker, his mind wrestling briefly with the painful prospect of losing half his hard-earned prize. Yet, feeling the growing ache in his strained muscles, he realized he had no other viable choice remaining.

Slowly, his fingers relaxed their fierce tension, allowing several of the round brown filberts to tumble free and scatter across the table. As the volume of his captured treasure shrank, the shape of his fist altered instantly within the narrow glass neck. The bulky mass dissolved into a manageable size, and with a sudden, smooth motion, his hand slipped effortlessly out of the container. He staggered backward a step, rubbing his sore wrist, staring in astonishment at the small handful of nuts that remained in his palm. He was completely free at last, and the remaining food was more than enough to satisfy his hunger.

That singular afternoon left an indelible mark upon the growing boy, shaping his understanding of the world long after the tears had dried. As the years progressed and he encountered new trials, the memory of his stuck hand returned to him with comforting clarity. Whenever ambition threatened to overwhelm his judgment, he would recall the narrow neck of the jar and the folly of holding on too tightly. Life presented countless corridors of choice, and he learned that true wisdom lay in knowing what to release. The simple domestic incident became a permanent compass for his moral and personal decisions.

The wisdom born from such everyday mistakes has traveled across generations, preserved in the oral traditions of thoughtful communities everywhere. When children hear this timeless narrative, they recognize the dangerous nature of unbridled appetite long before they face the harsher trials of adulthood. A society that values moderation avoids the needless suffering brought about by excess and blind ambition. The kind friend in the house demonstrated that complex human struggles often yield to the simplest truths when properly applied. Therefore, attentive listeners always cherish the quiet guidance offered by those who have walked the path before them.

Ultimately, the story of the boy and the filberts remains a quiet monument to human nature and the art of living well. It reminds every passerby that freedom and peace are infinitely more valuable than the accumulation of unnecessary burdens. As long as people gather to share stories in the fading evening light, this cautionary tale will continue to offer its gentle instruction. Let us therefore keep our desires measured and our minds open to the simple truths that surround us daily. In doing so, we navigate the complexities of our existence with grace, ensuring that our hands remain free for whatever truly matters.
